title: Whole-House Carpet Installation in Kirkland: A Real Cost Example
meta: Whole-house carpet in Kirkland, itemized: 1,150 sq ft at $0.99 per sq ft labor, 14 stairs at $30 a step, plus carpet and pad quoted at the free estimate.
keywords: whole house carpet installation cost, how much carpet for a whole house, carpet installation quote breakdown, carpet cost example, carpet installation Kirkland WA

blocks.lead: A whole-house carpet job is six lines, and three of them are published: stretch-in labor at $0.99 per sq ft, stairs at $30 per step, and pulling the old carpet and pad out at $0.45 per sq ft.
blocks.detail: The house below is a real Kirkland two-story with 1,150 sq ft of carpet and 14 steps: 1,150 × $0.99 + 14 × $30 = $1,558.50 in labor, plus $517.50 for tear-out. The carpet and pad are quoted at the free estimate and are still the biggest line on the page.

blocks.html: The house in this example is a real type we see constantly on the Eastside: a 1988 two-story in Juanita with a carpeted upstairs, carpeted family room and a straight staircase, being recarpeted before a family moves in. The same layout shows up across Finn Hill, Rose Hill and the newer parts of Totem Lake. Kirkland buyers expect carpet that belongs in a house at that price, which is why the fiber and pad here sit mid-range rather than at the bottom.

items.text: Carpet is sold from 12 ft rolls in square yards. Widths that do not fit the roll create seams and offcuts, so the order runs about 12 percent above the floor area.

blocks.text: Step three: the same house at three spec levels

items.title: Polyester cut pile, 6 lb pad
items.text: The lowest material line and a fine choice for a rental or a quick pre-sale refresh. Softer underfoot at first, but it mats in the hall and on the stairs within a few years. Keep it in the bedrooms and put something tougher on the stairs.

items.title: Mid-grade nylon, 8 lb pad
items.text: Resilient enough for a family and a dog, holds its texture on the staircase, and reads as quality to a Kirkland buyer. The material line rises by roughly a third over polyester and the pad by a little, while the $1,558.50 of labor does not move. This is the sweet spot for most Juanita and Finn Hill homes.

items.title: Wool or patterned nylon, upgraded pad
items.text: For a Houghton or Bridle Trails home where the carpet is a design feature. Wool or a patterned loop can double the material line, and patterns add waste for matching. Worth it in a primary suite, rarely in kids' rooms.

blocks.note: Labor, stairs and tear-out are identical in all three: $1,558.50 plus $517.50 on this house. The entire difference between these columns is the carpet and the pad.

blocks.title: Why the labor number is firm and the material number is not:
blocks.text: Two Kirkland houses of the same size get the same $0.99 per sq ft, the same $30 a step and the same $0.45 tear-out. What separates them is the carpet and pad, which can differ by half on identical square footage. That is the number we will not guess at over the phone.
Mistakes that make a whole-house job cost more than it should

items.html: Ordering from room dimensions instead of a seam diagram. Carpet comes 12 ft wide, so a 13 ft room needs a seam and an extra strip. See how to measure for carpet before you order anything.
Putting the cheapest carpet on the stairs. Stairs take the most wear in the house. If the budget is tight, save in the guest room, not on the staircase.
Reusing the old pad. Pad is a small line and it decides how the carpet feels and how long it lasts. Old pad also holds a decade of dust and pet history.
Recarpeting room by room over two years. Dye lots change, the 500 sq ft minimum repeats, and you pay setup twice. One order, one install, one seam diagram.
Skipping the subfloor check. Pulling 1980s carpet in Juanita sometimes finds squeaks and stained particleboard. Finding it at the estimate keeps it off the install-day invoice.

blocks.text: What to have ready for the measure

items: A list of every room and closet getting carpet, and which rooms are staying hard-surface.
The stair count, and whether any steps are open on one side or pie-shaped.
Where pets sleep, so the pad upgrade goes in the right room.
Whether the house will be empty or furnished on install day.
Your budget priority: softest feel, longest life, or lowest total. It changes the fiber we bring.

faq.q: How is whole-house carpet measured and priced?
faq.a: Room by room, in square feet converted to square yards, with a seam diagram for the 12 ft roll width. Labor is $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in, so 1,150 sq ft is $1,138.50, plus $30 per step, $0.45 per sq ft for tear-out and $0.25 if we move furniture. Carpet and pad are quoted separately.

faq.q: What is the biggest cost in a whole-house carpet job?
faq.a: The carpet material, usually about half the total and the one line we cannot publish. Labor on this house is a fixed $1,558.50 including the 14 stairs. The fiber moves the material line more than anything else: polyester is the least, nylon roughly a third more, wool or patterned carpet double or more.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to carpet the whole house at once?
faq.a: Yes. One roll order, one setup and one seam plan cost less than doing rooms over two years, and the 500 sq ft labor minimum only applies once. A single 300 sq ft bedroom still bills at 500 × $0.99 = $495, so small jobs pay for area they do not use.

faq.q: How much extra carpet is needed for waste?
faq.a: Usually 10 to 15 percent above the floor area, depending on how room widths fit the 12 ft roll and where seams fall. Patterned carpet needs more for pattern matching. The quote should show the square yards ordered, not just the floor area.

faq.q: Should the stairs get the same carpet as the bedrooms?
faq.a: Usually the same color for a continuous look, but the stairs should be at least as durable as anything in the house. If the bedrooms get polyester on a budget, put nylon on the staircase. Stairs are $30 per step, 14 of them here, and open-sided steps take longer to wrap.

faq.q: How long does a whole-house carpet installation take in Kirkland?
faq.a: Two days for a typical two-story like the example: upstairs and stairs the first day, main floor the second. An empty house goes faster. Furniture moving, at $0.25 per sq ft, and old carpet removal both add time, and we confirm the schedule when we hand you the quote.
